title: The Whole Summer
premise: After a humiliating collapse mid-concert, cellist Marguerite Nystrom retreats to her late grandmother's island orchard, only to discover the deed names a co-owner: Elias Brandt, the boy who left her fifteen years ago and is now the investor whose money saved her orchestra. Forced to share one stubborn summer on the island, they restore the orchard and each other while her comeback audition and his company's buyout deadline close in. At the last ferry of the season, Marguerite must choose between the career that saved her and the belonging she finally sees clearly — and Elias must prove the deed was never about the land.
about_author: Jonah Winterbourne is the pen name of a former orchard worker who spent six summers on an island ferry route before turning to fiction. He writes love stories about people who arrive late and stay anyway.

chapters.title: The Broken String
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Mid-solo at her career-defining concert, her hands seize and the hall goes silent. In the aftermath, her agent offers a leave of absence that sounds like an ending. Emotional beat: public humiliation and the terror that her identity died on that stage.

chapters.title: Paper and Thorns
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She arrives at her grandmother's island orchard to hide, but the ferry clerk mentions the property changed hands. At the county office she finds a deed with two names: hers and Elias Brandt's. Emotional beat: shock hardening into resolve — she won't be pushed off another stage.

chapters.title: The Man Off the Ferry
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias steps off the last afternoon boat expecting an empty property and a fast signature. Instead he finds Marguerite, furious, blocking the gate. Their fifteen-year silence breaks badly. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as businesslike calm.

chapters.title: Terms of Possession
chapters.summary: Dual POV. They strike a grudging deal: split the summer, split the harvest, then sell and never speak again. Marguerite sets rules; Elias agrees too easily. Emotional beat: a truce that neither believes in.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Clearing storm-damaged rows, she finds her grandmother's grafting journal and learns Elias visited the orchard the winter before she did — and paid its back taxes. Emotional beat: the first crack in her anger.

chapters.title: The Investor's Secret
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A call from his firm reveals his buyout fund is circling the island's waterfront — including this orchard. He hides it, telling himself he'll fix it. Emotional beat: the old habit of leaving before he can be left.

chapters.title: Practice in the Barn
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Unable to resist the barn's acoustics, she plays for the first time since the collapse — and freezes at the same passage. Elias, fixing the roof above, listens without a word. Emotional beat: grief surfacing where she can't control it.

chapters.title: Cider and Confessions
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Pressing the first apples, Elias admits why he left at nineteen: his father's bankruptcy, a forged signature, shame. Marguerite reveals her hands failed the year her mother died. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing the price each paid.

chapters.title: The Ferry Schedule
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Her agent calls: the audition for principal cellist is in six weeks — days before the last ferry. Elias's firm demands his return the same week. Emotional beat: time becoming the antagonist.

chapters.title: Grafting
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Following the journal, they graft new stock together, Elias's steady hands guiding hers. A near-kiss at the workbench is interrupted by a letter: the orchard is flagged for the waterfront buyout. Emotional beat: tenderness interrupted by dread.

chapters.title: What Elias Knew
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She discovers Elias's fund authored the buyout — and that he signed the deed knowing, possibly to shield her from a worse buyer. Feeling played either way, she locks the barn. Emotional beat: betrayal layered over love.

chapters.title: The Empty Dock
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias confronts his partners and stalls the buyout at the cost of his career's safety net. He returns to find the orchard dark and Marguerite's cello case gone. Emotional beat: choosing her before knowing if she'll choose him.

chapters.title: Storm Row
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. A night storm threatens the young grafts; Marguerite works the rows alone until Elias appears, soaked, and they save the trees in silence. Afterwards, in the barn, they finally kiss. Emotional beat: surrender in the middle of ruin.

chapters.title: The Audition Tape
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias secretly records Marguerite playing the storm-repaired orchard at dawn — flawless, free — and sends it to her agent without asking. Emotional beat: love as interference, however well-meant.

chapters.title: Second Betrayal
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite learns of the tape and explodes: everyone keeps deciding what she can survive. She tells Elias to take his signature and go. Emotional beat: the collapse repeating as a choice — pushing away before failing again.

chapters.title: The Deed's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Reviewing the old deed with the county clerk, Elias finds his father's forged signature from fifteen years ago was on this same property — the debt that broke his family began here. He understands what his grandmother and hers were trying to mend. Emotional beat: the past reframing everything.

chapters.title: What Marguerite Sees
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Playing again at dawn, alone, Marguerite realizes her hands didn't fail from grief but from a life with nothing in it but the career. The orchard, the trees, Elias — that was the missing resonance. Emotional beat: clarity arriving like tuning.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Audition day and the final boat collide. Marguerite plays the audition — and wins — then runs for the dock as the ferry pulls out. Elias is on it, having signed the orchard wholly over to her. Emotional beat: everything won, everything about to be lost.

chapters.title: Over Water
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite flags a fishing skiff and chases the ferry, standing in the bow playing the passage that once broke her — playing it whole. Passengers pull Elias to the rail. Emotional beat: triumph and pursuit braided into one gesture.

chapters.title: The Second Signature
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. At the dock, Elias shows her the deed: he didn't sign it away — he added a clause making it theirs jointly, unbreakable, like his grandmother intended. He asks for nothing but to stay. Emotional beat: the grand gesture undone into something humbler and truer.

chapters.title: Harvest
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Weeks later, the island harvest festival: Marguerite plays in the barn for neighbors, principal cellist by title, islander by choice, with a teaching studio and a season split she designed herself. Elias presses cider beside her. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not stumbled into.

chapters.title: The Whole Summer
chapters.summary: Dual POV, alternating short passages. On the first frost morning they walk the orchard rows, reading the grandmother's journal's final line aloud together: plant what outlives you. The ferry horn sounds for the last crossing of the year, and neither of them looks up. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace — the price paid, the memory kept.
